title: IETF SCITT RFC 9424 and AI Supply-Chain Attestation -- Turning Model Claims Into Verifiable Evidence
context: 2026-08-28 -- SCITT architecture is standardized; AI model and dataset attestation drafts are advancing through the working group
body: The IETF SCITT working group (Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust) standardizes how claims about a digital artifact -- who built it, how it was tested, what it contains -- are recorded so any later party can verify them without trusting the claimant. RFC 9424 defines the architecture: a transparency service holds a tamper-evident ledger of signed statements about software and, increasingly, AI model artifacts, training datasets, and benchmark results. This matters for AI governance because a self-attested safety claim is weak, while a signed statement about a measured benchmark run, anchored to a specific model artifact hash, is strong. The Council of AI aligns its verified measurement credential with SCITT: each 14-axis measurement run is recorded as a signed statement over the artifact, so a model's performance and containment posture can be checked against an immutable transparency service instead of a marketing page. Key near-term steps for operators: (1) compute and record content hashes for every shipped model and dataset; (2) attach signed measurement statements to those hashes; (3) point procurement and audit teams at the transparency ledger, so 'trusted' is replaced by 'verifiable'.
